Subject: Observability activation: LogiCo production onboarding

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. The execs signed off on the Dedicated plan and we want to start telemetry activation next week. High-level asks: dashboards for token-level cost by service, tracing hooks for inference latency, error taxonomy for model fallbacks, and an initial alert routing map so our SREs know who to page.

Two constraints to call out: 
- We have an internal requirement to keep PII out of logs (we'll provide a scrubbing list).
- Our traffic pattern spikes around 03:00 UTC daily; keeping tail latency under 180ms is important.

Can you send a short activation plan and recommend which of your runbook templates we should use?

Thanks,
Elena

Head of Platform
LogiCo

Elena —

Great news on the Dedicated sign-off, and thanks for the constraints list. Short plan below, we can flesh timelines once your SREs confirm a kickoff slot: 

1) Intake & scope (Day 0): confirmed scrubbing list, service list, and primary SRE oncall.
2) Instrumentation pass (Day 1-2): tracing hooks + KV cache metrics + per-route token counters. Aditya will propose the minimal SDK changes.
3) Dashboard build (Day 2-4): cost-by-service, 99/95 latency panels, model fallback rates. We'll use a shared Grafana folder for easy handover.
4) Error taxonomy & runbook (Day 3): classify errors (client, model, infra, rate-limit) and draft runbook pages for each. Grace will map alert routing (pager and slack).
5) Canary + load validation (Day 5-7): exercise prefix caching and observe tail latency under production-like spike.

Deliverables: onboarding checklist, runbook draft, Grafana folder, tracing hook spec, and a short validation report.

Can you confirm availability for a 60-min kickoff on Monday (10/16) at 10:00 PT? If so we will attach the checklist and the runbook template pre-meeting.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-onboard-checklist.xlsx, runbook-template-v1.md
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Observability activation: LogiCo production onboarding

Elena / Team —

Quick technical note on the tracing hooks:
- We recommend instrumenting at these points:
  * request entry (service ingress) — capture request id, user_id hash (no raw PII), model id, route id
  * pre-inference queue latency — time in queue per request
  * KV cache hit/miss event with key namespace
  * model token streaming start/end timestamps
  * inference result code (OK / MODEL_FALLBACK / TIMEOUT / RATE_LIMIT)

- Sample rates: start with 10% head sampling + error-only full traces for the first week. This reduces overhead while giving visibility into rare tail events.
- We'll produce a CSV with the hook names and suggested JSON payload fields (attached: logico-tracing-hooks.csv).

Note on PII: we'll include a redaction layer in the SDK and provide a pre-commit linter rule for instrumented code to avoid accidental logging.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Aditya —

I'll own the error taxonomy + alert routing. Proposed taxonomy (short):
- client_error: invalid inputs, bad schema (notify App team)
- model_error: model output failures, decoding errors (notify ML Ops)
- performance_degradation: p99/p95 breach, increased queue time (notify SRE)
- fallback_event: model fallback to smaller variant (notify Product + CS)
- security_violation: PII leak detect (notify Security + Legal)

Alert routing rules:
- pages for performance_degradation (pager duty → SRE primary) and security_violation (pager duty → Security IR).
- emails/slack for model_error and fallback_event to ML Ops and Product with a 5-min aggregation window to cut noise.
- runbook entry for each taxonomy item with severity levels and rollback steps. I'll draft pages in runbook-template-v1.md and push to the shared Drive before the kickoff.

I'll also include escalation steps if the canary fails: immediate fallback to read-only traffic on the Redwood Dedicated pool and a short incident template.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Ops Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
